newsitem.title: ZIMBABWE: World Bank to help Zimbabwe gather economic data.
newsitem.headline: World Bank to help Zimbabwe gather economic data.

text.p: The World Bank will next year help Zimbabwe improve its economic data collection, a bank official said on Friday.

Kapil Kapoor, World Bank deputy representative in Harare, said the project would also involve the International Monetary Fund (IMF) and the British Overseas Development Agency (ODA), and was aimed at ensuring information published by the state Central Statistical Office (CSO) was accurate and up-to-date.
Zimbabwean economists have for years called for an improvement in data gathering.

"The key problem when one is looking at GDP growth in Zimbabwe is that some economic indicators are not captured through the CSO, particularly information on the contribution of new entrants to businesses to growth," Kapoor told reporters.

"That is why we have decided on a programme where a team of experts will assist the CSO to estimate GDP growth taking into account some of the new companies formed and other entrants into the economy such as the informal sector," he added.
